subject: How we can help save our planet for Earth Day:
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY WELCH FOR VERMONT
body:
On Earth Day and every day, we need to keep up the fight for a Green New Deal.

# [](https://act.welchforvermont.com/go/144?t=2&akid=277%2E61531%2Etv4uyC)
Hello,
Tomorrow is Earth Day, and I wanted to send you an early message about what this holiday means to me, our state, and our campaign.
I like to take an extra minute on Earth Day to appreciate Vermont’s natural beauty. I can walk out my front door and go on a hike (or cross country ski in the winter, but I’m hopeful we’re done with the snow for now). It’s a true wonder of our state, and I’m thankful for it every day.
Earth Day also reminds us of the importance of a Green New Deal, and why we need to get it passed and onto President Biden’s desk immediately. Vermonters and all Americans rely on a healthy environment, and if we’re going to ensure future generations have the same access to the great outdoors, we must act now.
We can confront climate change and create millions of good-paying jobs at the same time. I’m an original cosponsor of the Green New Deal—now we must work together to get it done.
[**Add your name to our petition today if you agree that Congress must pass the Green New Deal right away.**](https://act.welchforvermont.com/signup/em-green-new-deal/?source=em_20220421_f_p_earthday&t=4&akid=277%2E61531%2Etv4uyC)
It’s easy to be frustrated by the state of our environment. But there’s good news: We’ve led the way and innovated solutions to tackle some of our most troubling environmental challenges in the past, and we can do it again.
Unfortunately, even though the stakes are so high, so many of my Republican colleagues are either avoiding the issue or denying it exists altogether. But we don’t have time to waste—we must act now if we’re going to protect the planet for generations to come.
[**In honor of Earth Day, please add your name to our petition and say you support for a Green New Deal.** ](https://act.welchforvermont.com/signup/em-green-new-deal/?source=em_20220421_f_p_earthday&t=5&akid=277%2E61531%2Etv4uyC)
Thanks for taking action,
Peter

Are you taking this seriously?! | | **_[Friend, the GOP’s relentless attacks on science are only growing worse. QUICKLY: Sign our petition to condemn Republicans' anti-science agenda>>>](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/44401343/341424461/280682659?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85MzUzMiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhNzdjZTZlNy1iYmMxLWVjMTEtOTk3ZS0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=z0d9oy20y7CVU5qC3W9cHuBjfr-4JfjM5IdxCgKSFPs=&emci=9e41a48c-b3c1-ec11-997e-281878b83d8a&emdi=a77ce6e7-bbc1-ec11-997e-281878b83d8a&ceid=5643049)_**

It doesn’t take a scientist to realize that Republicans are full of it.
We’ve all heard the talking points — “It’s cold outside, that means global warming can’t be real,” and “climate change is natural,” or how about “climate change is a hoax.”
Wrong, wrong, and wrong again.
It’s no secret that the Earth is getting warmer, sea levels are rising, and wildfires are growing rampant. **But the bigger problem is that right-wing politicians put fossil fuel lobbyists above the future of our planet._And they’re getting away with it._**
Oil companies like Exxon — which knew about climate change more than 40 years ago! — refuse to be accountable and promote misinformation instead.
And these lawmakers let them! They’d rather attack science and undermine the experts, so long as it lines their pockets.
The truth is there is no longer time to just “study the issue.” No time for half-measures. It’s time for bold action to save the planet. Nothing short of a massive, sustained, crisis-level investment — coordinated with the rest of the world — can hope to save us.
I don’t know about you, but I am not staying silent as the GOP prolongs this crisis.

name: Rachel Patterson, Evergreen Action
subject: Addressing environmental racism without race?
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY EVERGREEN ACTION
body:
Sign an official public comment for environmental justice right now.
| [](https://act.evergreenaction.com/letter/tell-biden-admin-address-environmental-racism/?utm_source=ema_2022-04-21_biden_admin_enviro_racism_ej_tool_comment_&source=ema_2022-04-21_biden_admin_enviro_racism_ej_tool_comment_&t=2&akid=12965%2E53494%2EakzwII) Friend, On the campaign trail, Joe Biden made a bold promise to direct 40% of the benefits from clean energy investments to communities that have suffered environmental injustice. The Council on Environmental Quality just took the first step toward fulfilling this promise—identifying those communities with a new Climate and Economic Justice Screening Tool. But there's a huge piece missing: **The current proposed tool to address environmental racism does not consider race.** Luckily, they just opened a public comment period. This is our chance to encourage their progress and call for a stronger, more just screening tool. [**_Will you join us and sign an official public comment right now? We'll submit it directly to decision-makers for you._**](https://act.evergreenaction.com/letter/tell-biden-admin-address-environmental-racism/?utm_source=ema_2022-04-21_biden_admin_enviro_racism_ej_tool_comment_&source=ema_2022-04-21_biden_admin_enviro_racism_ej_tool_comment_&t=3&akid=12965%2E53494%2EakzwII) | [SIGN ON](https://act.evergreenaction.com/letter/tell-biden-admin-address-environmental-racism/?utm_source=ema_2022-04-21_biden_admin_enviro_racism_ej_tool_comment_&source=ema_2022-04-21_biden_admin_enviro_racism_ej_tool_comment_&t=4&akid=12965%2E53494%2EakzwII)
---
If the Council on Environmental Quality proceeds with the current version of this screening tool, it will have adverse consequences.
By focusing only on criteria like education level and income, the screening tool misses the fact that **communities of color face more pollution than their white counterparts _at every socioeconomic level._**
Take a middle-income Black community that experiences disproportionate pollution, for example. The proposed screening tool wouldn't count this community as disadvantaged and would deny them the funds.
[**_The Biden administration must face environmental racism head-on. Sign an official public comment and make sure this critical new policy achieves its full potential!_**](https://act.evergreenaction.com/letter/tell-biden-admin-address-environmental-racism/?utm_source=ema_2022-04-21_biden_admin_enviro_racism_ej_tool_comment_&source=ema_2022-04-21_biden_admin_enviro_racism_ej_tool_comment_&t=5&akid=12965%2E53494%2EakzwII)
Together,
Rachel Patterson
Policy Lead, Evergreen Action

# Ed's Thoughts on Debates
---
| | |
Who needs debates in a time where 30-second advertisements funded by multinational corporations will suffice? Yes, it's true, the Governor and Lt. Governor refused to participate in the debates. Three of us were invited by the Idaho Debate Commission to participate in the long-standing and cherished tradition. Unfortunately, both of my opponents retreated from the free exchange of ideas. This is a dangerous trend for Idaho.
If we allow candidates to avoid constituents and opponents, then the domination of giant corporations over government will be complete. We're swamped by political theater manufactured by master manipulators. Nothing seems real anymore. There is a constant barrage of advertisements making candidates look competent and "Conservative" (without them ever defining that word). It's just easier to do it that way. Special interest groups do not like preparing their chosen candidates for the debate stage because it's one environment where candidates' artificially polished image is at risk.
However, Idahoans deserve to witness the contest of ideas. It's through that contest where ideas are improved. Competing visions give Idahoans a glimpse into what our future can be. It's a time to aspire to greater heights. Sure, it's also a time where we can look back on where we've been and openly discuss how we could have done better. Anyone who claims they are motivated for Idahoans best interest should celebrate that, not condemn it!
Sadly, we see how these elections have turned into nothing more than career politicians perpetuating their political careers. Idaho is at a fork in the road. The future of our state is a discussion worth having. I call on my opponents to consider the best interest of our state. If you care about Idaho, you should care about participating in the electoral process in a more meaningful way than only pushing 30-second ads funded by special interest groups.
-Ed Humphreys

body:
|
# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/44402685/341430686/390307162?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTYyOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmZTJhZWQ5Yi1jMmMxLWVjMTEtOTk3ZS0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=l21YkiSDQFXWsq9QW__BG4aE6rTLLXo2eRoKuenUCr0=)
Friend,

I often talk about Doug LaMalfa, but today I’m going to take a step back and talk about the Republican Party’s plans for our country if they win in 2022.

Short summary:_it’s bad..._

Republican Senator Rick Scott recently published an “11-Point Plan” for America if the GOP takes back control. In the interest of brevity, I’m only going to talk about the sixth point -- which addresses the economy and government spending.

Point six opens up with a doozy: **_“Enact term limits for the Washington ruling class – 12-year limits for Congress and government bureaucrats"_**
They might as well come out and say they want to destroy the Civil Service. 12 years is not enough time for managers to learn their jobs. If the idea is to “make government more efficient”, firing people who know what they’re doing is the opposite of a good plan. For example, I was a diplomat. Career Ambassadors -- as opposed to “political” Ambassadors who “buy” a cushy post to Europe with campaign donations -- spend 25 years or more working their way through the Foreign Service. This experience is invaluable, and there is no “private sector” analogue. The GOP plan would cripple American diplomacy, and many of the government agencies we rely on here at home. It would be a disaster.

That’s not all though. Here's another piece of the plan:
**_“All federal legislation will sunset in 5 years. If a law is worth keeping, Congress can pass it again.”_**
That innocuous-sounding sentence means that Social Security and Medicare would always be five years from ending. Republicans have been trying to gut entitlements for decades -- this is their next attempt. Real Americans rely on these programs, but Republicans will cut whatever it takes to lower taxes for their rich donors.

Speaking of reducing the tax burden on the rich, the GOP plan also proposes to:
**_“Immediately cut the IRS funding and workforce by 50%.”_**
That’s a pure give-away to rich Americans who have the most incentive and the means to cheat on their taxes. Here’s the fact: every dollar spent on the IRS MAKES two more dollars through increased enforcement. It’s the best spending the government can do from a “balanced budget” perspective. The GOP doesn’t want to “balance the budget” though. They want to serve the rich.

It doesn't stop there! Another bullet says that:
**_“If government fails to comply with the law, citizens must have the right to sue to force them to comply.”_**
That sounds fine, until you realize that only rich people will be able to afford the lawyer fees to challenge the government. This epitomizes the GOP dream of government in a nutshell: a government that makes rules for the common man but not the wealthy aristocracy. The GOP wants their wealthy donor class to be above the law. It is a disgrace.

I could go on. For example, the GOP plan also includes provisions to sell public land to the highest bidder (ie, the rich), and plans to privatize the Veteran’s Administration under the guise of “choice”. But this email has gone on long enough, and I encourage you to check the plan out if you’re curious, here: [https://rescueamerica.com/steps/6-government-reform-debt/](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/44402686/341430687/720604956?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTYyOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmZTJhZWQ5Yi1jMmMxLWVjMTEtOTk3ZS0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=l21YkiSDQFXWsq9QW__BG4aE6rTLLXo2eRoKuenUCr0=)

This is a plan to destroy America as we know it, and we need to stop the Republican Party. To do that, I need your support.

Thanks in advance for anything you can afford.

Max Steiner

clean_body: | = Friend, I often talk about Doug LaMalfa, but today I’m going to take a step back and talk about the Republican Party’s plans for our country if they win in 2022. Short summary:it’s bad... Republican Senator Rick Scott recently published an “11-Point Plan” for America if the GOP takes back control. In the interest of brevity, I’m only going to talk about the sixth point -- which addresses the economy and government spending. Point six opens up with a doozy: “Enact term limits for the Washington ruling class – 12-year limits for Congress and government bureaucrats" They might as well come out and say they want to destroy the Civil Service. 12 years is not enough time for managers to learn their jobs. If the idea is to “make government more efficient”, firing people who know what they’re doing is the opposite of a good plan. For example, I was a diplomat. Career Ambassadors -- as opposed to “political” Ambassadors who “buy” a cushy post to Europe with campaign donations -- spend 25 years or more working their way through the Foreign Service. This experience is invaluable, and there is no “private sector” analogue. The GOP plan would cripple American diplomacy, and many of the government agencies we rely on here at home. It would be a disaster. That’s not all though. Here's another piece of the plan: “All federal legislation will sunset in 5 years. If a law is worth keeping, Congress can pass it again.” That innocuous-sounding sentence means that Social Security and Medicare would always be five years from ending. Republicans have been trying to gut entitlements for decades -- this is their next attempt. Real Americans rely on these programs, but Republicans will cut whatever it takes to lower taxes for their rich donors. Speaking of reducing the tax burden on the rich, the GOP plan also proposes to: “Immediately cut the IRS funding and workforce by 50%.” That’s a pure give-away to rich Americans who have the most incentive and the means to cheat on their taxes. Here’s the fact: every dollar spent on the IRS MAKES two more dollars through increased enforcement. It’s the best spending the government can do from a “balanced budget” perspective. The GOP doesn’t want to “balance the budget” though. They want to serve the rich. It doesn't stop there! Another bullet says that: “If government fails to comply with the law, citizens must have the right to sue to force them to comply.” That sounds fine, until you realize that only rich people will be able to afford the lawyer fees to challenge the government. This epitomizes the GOP dream of government in a nutshell: a government that makes rules for the common man but not the wealthy aristocracy. The GOP wants their wealthy donor class to be above the law. It is a disgrace. I could go on. For example, the GOP plan also includes provisions to sell public land to the highest bidder (ie, the rich), and plans to privatize the Veteran’s Administration under the guise of “choice”. Peter,

I have to admit - I hadn't heard of the far-left publication called _The Nation_ before last week. Now, I'll never forget it.

They published an attack piece against me - based on the color of my skin - that is beyond ridiculous and insulting.

While I'm personally very offended, I'm genuinely sad for the author of this political hit piece.

There are a lot of nasty things said about me in this article simply because I'm a Black Republican. Like this:

"Herschel Walker, the football star turned Georgia Senate candidate, is an animated caricature of a Black person drawn by white conservatives."
Or maybe this line:

"Herschel Walker's candidacy is a white insult to Black people."
It's shameful.

But the writer doesn't just take aim at me. He questions the support from folks like you, too:

"Most white people in the South vote 'R' like their entire white supremacist project depends on it."
Peter, I never wanted the color of my skin to be a focal point of this Senate campaign. However, can you imagine the reaction from the mainstream media if these things had been said about a Black Democrat? The outrage! There would be calls for the writer to be fired and the publication cancelled.

But I'm not calling for a protest of the author or a boycott of the publication's advertisers. Nothing like that.

_**I think the best answer is to prove them wrong at the ballot box.**_

While I'm personally very offended, I'm genuinely sad for the author of this political hit piece. | Peter, I have to admit - I hadn't heard of the far-left publication called The Nation before last week. Now, I'll never forget it. They published an attack piece against me - based on the color of my skin - that is beyond ridiculous and insulting. While I'm personally very offended, I'm genuinely sad for the author of this political hit piece. There are a lot of nasty things said about me in this article simply because I'm a Black Republican. Like this: "Herschel Walker, the football star turned Georgia Senate candidate, is an animated caricature of a Black person drawn by white conservatives." Or maybe this line: "Herschel Walker's candidacy is a white insult to Black people." It's shameful. But the writer doesn't just take aim at me. He questions the support from folks like you, too: "Most white people in the South vote 'R' like their entire white supremacist project depends on it." Peter, I never wanted the color of my skin to be a focal point of this Senate campaign. However, can you imagine the reaction from the mainstream media if these things had been said about a Black Democrat? The outrage! There would be calls for the writer to be fired and the publication cancelled. But I'm not calling for a protest of the author or a boycott of the publication's advertisers. Nothing like that. I think the best answer is to prove them wrong at the ballot box. The media has been against our campaign since we launched last summer, but they have rarely been so brazen to say things as this: "Georgia Republicans want Walker because he's Black and Warnock is Black, and they think they can defeat Warnock in November if they can shave just a little of the Black vote..." body:
We’re proud to stand behind Amanda Edwards as the next mayor of Houston, and here are a few reasons why: | | | Team, **Allow us to introduce you to Amanda K. Edwards.** Amanda is a proud native of Houston, a graduate of Emory University and Harvard Law School, a former member of the Houston City Council, and now she is running to be the next Mayor of Houston. We’re proud to stand behind Amanda as the next mayor of Houston, and here are a few reasons why:
* She is a **transformative and innovative leader** who has worked to expand our tech and innovation ecosystem
* She has a **passion for public-service** , dedicating years of service to Houston as an At-Large member of the City Council and a strong civic leader
* She makes **solutions driven** , and has shown leadership for our community as a non-profit leader
* She is driven by her **commitment to empower communities** , working closely with women and minority-owned small businesses to get them the resources they need
* She has the **experience and skills** to address complicated city challenges like crime, flooding, and the city’s finances.

Minnesota non-profit organizations are collecting millions of your tax dollars and they need to be **held accountable for how they spend our money**.

This is a farce and folks know it

| [ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/44404931/341438335/-742096553?refcode=header-img&&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MjI4MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5ODE4YTdjOC1jY2MxLWVjMTEtOTk3ZS0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=oNcQc-6Vs_KUol-M4y1sUp-6I8EpK7BXJBmF6459E-Q=)

Peter, I wish I had better news to share with you. **_FLORIDA GOP VOTES TO APPROVE GERRYMANDERED REDISTRICTING MAP THAT SLASHES BLACK REPRESENTATION, DEMOCRATS FIGHT BACK_** I spent this morning in the House chamber exposing Ron DeSantis and his cronies’ blatant effort to cut Black representation and diminish the power of the Black vote in Florida. **I am proud to stand tall with my fellow Black Democrats in the face of this injustice.

I will not allow this moment to pass us by without making our voices heard.** I have my mother's blood and my father's blood coursing through my veins. I have my ancestors' blood coursing through my veins. They have fought too much for us to bury our heads in the sand.

\- **I have a vested interest in these maps because I represent Black Floridians.**
\- I have a vested interest because **I know the struggles of Black and Brown folks over the course of 200+ years in this country, but most certainly in this state.**
\- I have a vested interest because **I understand it wasn't until the Voting Rights Act that my parents were able to vote.**
\- I have a vested interest because **I'm a Black woman in the state of Florida.**
\- I have a vested interest because **I'm a Black resident in the state of Florida.**

These maps are a farce and folks know it. Republicans have told us privately that they know it and they are allowing the governor to get away with it.

**Republicans have forced Florida to be the microcosm of the erosion of democracy. Peter, we cannot allow this to stand.**

In solidarity,

_Michele Rayner_
